This chapter develops the transfer-semigroup realization of the projector-resolved seed calculus. A seed is propagated by a one-parameter semigroup, a Markov kernel, a normalized Bayesian transfer, a fractional spectral power, a Green operator, or a potential-weighted Feynman--Kac operator. Exact packet projectors resolve every transfer into input-output blocks, and the semigroup law becomes block convolution over intermediate packets. Coarse and fine generators are compared by a refinement defect. A Duhamel identity proves that this generator-level defect is exactly the source of the corresponding semigroup defect and gives a quantitative stability bound. In the stochastic realization, point-mass seeds generate random walks and continuous-time Markov evolution; exact lumpability is the vanishing of the same refinement defect. Conditional expectation is treated as a weighted orthogonal packet projector, with nested partitions producing martingale-difference packets. Bayesian conditioning is a normalized nonlinear operator. Its independent-data composition law, packet-evidence decomposition, stability bound, conjugate updates, and continuous likelihood flow are proved explicitly.  The Bayesian refinement conjecture is resolved in finite dimensions: for strictly positive likelihoods and at least two coarse packets, exact commutation for every prior is equivalent to blockwise-constant likelihoods up to global scale, and every failure factors through an explicit information-loss packet. Fractional powers are constructed packetwise through the spectral projectors of a positive operator, and the square-root semigroup is recovered by subordination. The fractional-naturality conjecture is also resolved for bounded nonnegative self-adjoint refinement systems: the fractional intertwining defect has an exact resolvent integral, a gap-free Hölder certificate, a sharper common-gap estimate, and a Duhamel semigroup bound. Green kernels, finite-difference Poisson problems, and second-order low-mode convergence provide the PDE realization. A finite-state Feynman--Kac formula is proved by path enumeration. Exact Schur--Feshbach elimination shows that discarded latent packets return as a frequency-dependent self-energy and, in time coordinates, as a memory kernel. Survival and hazard functions are generated by transient semigroups. The transfer-semigroup realization gives one common operator language to several subjects that are often presented separately. Markov propagation is linear transfer of a probability seed. Conditional expectation is stochastic projection. Bayesian conditioning is normalized nonlinear transfer, and its exact finite coarsening law is characterized by packetwise likelihood sufficiency. Fractional calculus is spectral packet reweighting, and bounded positive refinement defects transfer to fractional powers and fractional semigroups by explicit resolvent and Duhamel estimates. A Green operator reconstructs a field from source packets. Feynman--Kac propagation adds path weights to stochastic transfer. Schur--Feshbach elimination shows that hidden packets are not destroyed; they return through self-energy and memory. Survival and hazard are scalar reconstructions of a transient semigroup.
